title: Chicken, NS as part, baked, coated, skin/coating eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide. This product uses boneless breast or thigh meat, baked in the oven and coated with a crispy breading. The skin and coating are edible, adding flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken provides all essential amino acids required by the human body.
Baking retains more B‑vitamins compared to frying, where they can be lost.
The coating can be made from whole‑grain flour, breadcrumbs, or nut crumbs, increasing fiber content.
Chicken is one of the most affordable protein sources, making it accessible to many populations.
Various cultures season baked chicken with spices ranging from paprika to curry.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of baked chicken provides about 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked without excessive oil, chicken remains low in fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains niacin (B3), B6, and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, important for bones, immunity, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: High protein and moderate fiber from the coating help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella or Campylobacter. Cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Allergy to coating ingredients
items.content: If the breading contains wheat, soy, or dairy, it can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared breadings often contain added salt. Choose low‑sodium versions if you have hypertension.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Bread crumbs can raise blood sugar quickly, which is relevant for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked coated chicken can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, sandwiches, or used in tacos. The skin and coating are eaten together, providing crunch and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consuming.
